historical_references.reference: Adrielle, the daughter of the Roman consul Publius Valerius Publicola, was traditionally believed to have been the first Christian martyr in Rome. According to legend, she was a young virgin who refused to sacrifice to the pagan gods in honor of Emperor Nero's birthday. She was put in a red-hot brass bull and thrown into the Tiber River. Miraculously, she survived and was later beheaded. Her feast day is celebrated on February 3.

Adrielle de la Marche, also known as Adelaide of the Marches, was a duchess of Normandy in the 11th century. She was the daughter of Count William I of Normandy and was noted for her piety and charitable works. She founded several monasteries and hospitals, and was venerated as a saint after her death.
